name: Mazar-e-Quaid
address: Mazar-e-Quaid-e-Azam, M.A. Jinnah Road, Gurmandir, Jacob Lines, Jamshed Town, Karachi Division, Sindh 75000, Pakistan
description: Mazar-e-Quaid, also known as the Jinnah Mausoleum or National Mausoleum, is the final resting place of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder of Pakistan. Designed in a traditional style with a minor influence of modernist style, it was completed in 1971. The mausoleum complex also contains the tomb of Jinnah's sister Fatima Jinnah, as well as those of Liaquat Ali Khan and Nurul Amin.

notes: Coordinates and address verified via Nominatim. Neither carries a tourism/building tag. Overpass API was unavailable during this run (primary endpoint refused connections / HTTP 000; kumi mirror returned 'server busy'), so the canonical building way could not be cross-checked. No official/government page (Ministry of Heritage & Culture / Quaid-i-Azam Mazar Management Board / Sindh Culture Dept) publishes opening hours or ticket prices, so those are null rather than guessed. Public access to the interior has been subject to security restrictions per news reports, but no acceptable official source was found to state current entry conditions. Photo visually confirmed to depict the white-marble domed mausoleum.

name: Mohatta Palace
address: Mohatta Palace, Motilal Goverdhandas Road, Old Clifton, Saddar Town, Karachi Division, Sindh 75600, Pakistan
entryConditions: Photography not permitted inside the Museum. The Museum is also closed on public holidays and during Ramzan.
contact: Tel. 0092 21 35837669, 35374879 - 7 Hatim Alvi Road, Clifton, Karachi-75600, Pakistan
description: The Mohatta Palace (Qasr-e-Fatima) is a palace in Karachi's Clifton area that now operates as a museum. Designed by Ahmed Hussain Agha, it was built in 1927 as the summer home of Shivratan Mohatta, a Hindu Marwari businessman from what is now Rajasthan, India. It is built in the tradition of the stone palaces of Rajasthan, using pink Jodhpur stone combined with local yellow stone from nearby Gizri.
notes: Hours, admission prices, entry conditions and contact read verbatim from the museum's own official website (mohattapalacemuseum.com, 'Visit the Museum' page). The official page states 'Adults Rs. 30 only; Free for seniors, school students, children under 12'; some third-party listings quote Rs. 100 but those are not official and are not used here. OSM tags the way tourism=museum. Accessibility, facilities and family-suitability are not stated on the official page, so left null. Photo visually confirmed to depict the palace exterior; file is Public domain.

name: Frere Hall
address: Frere Hall, Civil Lines, Saddar Town, Karachi Division, Sindh 74400, Pakistan
subcategory: colonial-era building / public library & exhibition space
description: Frere Hall is a building in Karachi, Pakistan that dates from the early British colonial era in Sindh. Completed in 1865, it was originally intended to serve as Karachi's town hall. It now serves as an exhibition space and library.
notes: Coordinates verified via Nominatim (single hit, node tagged leisure=park named 'Frere Hall'). Managed by the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC). The only 'opening hours' on any kmc.gos.pk page is the site-wide KMC Head Office footer ('Mon - Fri: 9:00 am - 5:00 pm'), which is NOT Frere Hall's own hours; the official KMC tourism page lists Frere Hall but gives no per-attraction hours/tickets. Library timings circulating online (e.g. '10am-5pm Mon-Sat') appear only on social media / blogs, which are not acceptable sources, so hours are null. Photo visually confirmed to depict the Gothic/Indo-Saracenic Frere Hall building.

name: Empress Market
address: Empress Market, Shahrah-e-Liaquat (Frere Road), Saddar Bazaar, Fowler Lines, Saddar, Karachi Division, Sindh 75530, Pakistan
description: The Empress Market is a marketplace situated in the Saddar area of Karachi, Pakistan. The market traces its origins to the British Raj era, when it was first constructed. Today it is among the most popular and busy places for shopping in Karachi, selling condiments, fruit, vegetables and meat to stationery material, textiles and pets; the recreational Jahangir Park is located nearby.
notes: Coordinates verified via Nominatim; used the node tagged historic=marketplace (osm_id 3191210900). Two other co-located hits exist (amenity=marketplace node 4950372523 and a landuse=commercial way 681523985). It is a functioning public market managed/renovated by KMC; the official KMC 'Revamping of Empress Market' page describes restoration works but states no opening hours, ticket prices or contact, so those are null (it is a free-access public market, but no official source was found to state that explicitly). Photo visually confirmed to depict the market building and its Gothic clock tower.

name: Wazir Mansion
address: Wazir Mansion, Chaghla Street, Bunder Quarter, Karachi Division, Sindh 72500, Pakistan
description: Wazir Mansion, officially known as the Quaid-e-Azam Birthplace Museum, is a former family home in the Kharadar area of Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan. It is considered the birthplace of the country's founder, Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The house now serves as a museum and is managed by the Department of Archaeology and Museums.
notes: Coordinates verified via Nominatim (single hit, way tagged tourism=museum). The official government page (Department of Archaeology & Museums, doam.gov.pk/public/heritage-sites/798) describes the site but states NO opening hours, ticket prices, entry conditions, accessibility or facilities. DOAM's published contact is its Islamabad HQ (+92 51-9252516, info@doam.gov.pk, Sir Syed Memorial Building, Islamabad), which is the managing authority's general contact, not a site-specific one, so 'contact' is left null to avoid mis-attribution. OSM's town tag reads 'Lyari Town' which conflicts with the commonly cited Kharadar location; address kept close to the OSM display_name. Photo visually confirmed to depict the 3-storey yellow-and-red Wazir Mansion building.
